paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. Moses asks, "what does the LORD your God ask of you" (Deuteronomy 10:12), and the answer isn't a pile of fancy stuff. It's to fear Him, walk in His ways, love Him, and serve Him "with all your heart and with all your soul" (Deuteronomy 10:12). And the commands come "for your own good" (Deuteronomy 10:13), so this isn't a boss hiding a rule book in the break room.

Why can Israel trust that? Because the One asking owns "the heavens, even the highest heavens, and the earth and everything in it" (Deuteronomy 10:14), and still He set His affection on their fathers (Deuteronomy 10:15). He's "showing no partiality," He loves the foreigner, and He cares for the fatherless and widow (Deuteronomy 10:17-18). So love for Him shows up in how you treat people, and I think that's the part we skip first. Then Moses lays two roads in front of them: a blessing for obeying, a curse for following other gods (Deuteronomy 11:26-28).

So what does that mean for you, baker? Obedience is what love does when it remembers what the LORD has done, and Israel had seen it with their own eyes (Deuteronomy 11:7). Fix His words in your heart, talk about them at home and on the road, and don't drift one "five more minutes" at a time (Deuteronomy 11:18-19). The LORD isn't asking for a show. He's asking for all of you, and He's already given you everything first. And the sermon isn't over, because Moses is NOT done preaching.
